title: 1990 AMC 8 Problem 1
statement: What is the smallest sum of two \(3\)-digit numbers that can be obtained by placing each of the six digits \(4,\) \(5,\) \(6,\) \(7,\) \(8,\) \(9\) into one of the six boxes of a sum of two \(3\)-digit numbers?

solutions.text:
To make the sum small, the two smallest digits go in the hundreds places, the next two in the tens places, and the two largest in the units places.

One such arrangement is \(468 + 579 = 1047\), and every arrangement of this type gives the same sum.

Thus, the correct answer is C .
hints: A digit in the hundreds place counts \(100\) times, so put the smallest digits there
Hundreds digits should be \(4\) and \(5\), tens digits \(6\) and \(7\), units digits \(8\) and \(9\)
